channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Build $100 Million Waste-to-Energy Plant in Khorezm
item.description: A $100 million waste-to-energy plant is planned for construction in Uzbekistan's Khorezm region. South Korean company Green Hammer Co., Ltd. will invest in the facility, designed to process 800 tons of waste daily and generate 71 million kWh of electricity annually. The project is scheduled for implementation between 2026 and 2028.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea: Strategic Partnership Figures Highlight Trade Imbalance
item.description: Trade between Uzbekistan and South Korea reached $1.1 billion in January-July, with Uzbekistan's exports at $37.5 million and imports from South Korea at $1.037 billion. This imbalance is attributed to Uzbekistan's demand for high-tech equipment. South Korea invested $216.4 million in Uzbekistan during January-June, with 730 Korean-capitalized enterprises operating in the country.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Discusses Airport Cooperation with South Korean Firm
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Kim Beom Ho, acting president of Incheon International Airport Corporation, in South Korea. They discussed modernizing Urgench airport and building a new Tashkent airport. The Korean firm plans to open an office in Tashkent, potentially becoming a center for airport management and training.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Gradual Increase in Retirement Age
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Economy and Finance has proposed gradually increasing the retirement age from 60 to 63 for men and from 55 to 58 for women. The plan involves a three-month annual increase starting in 2028, aiming for completion by 2039. The proposal is currently open for public discussion until September 30.

item.title: Uzbekistan Expands Criminal Liability for Interfering with Investigations and Court Cases
item.description: Uzbekistan has expanded criminal liability for interfering with investigations and court proceedings. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev signed a law clarifying penalties for influencing investigators, prosecutors, and judges. The law also broadens administrative liability for contempt of court and takes effect September 12.

item.title: Uzbek President Attends Uzbek-Korean Business Forum, Proposes Joint Economic Growth Initiatives
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and South Korean Prime Minister Han Duck-soo participated in an Uzbek-Korean business forum in Tashkent. Over 300 representatives from government and business attended. President Mirziyoyev highlighted Korea as a strategic partner and proposed combining resources, technology, and capital for new economic growth points.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's mining potential presented to British businesses in Bishkek
item.description: British companies learned about Kyrgyzstan's investment climate and mining sector changes at a meeting in Bishkek. UK engineering and consulting firms offered solutions in exploration, processing, and environmental safety. Experts discussed the country's mineral resources and licensing, noting a significant increase in foreign investment in mining.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov arrives in South Korea for official visit
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov arrived in South Korea for an official visit, where he was met by high-ranking officials. He is scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with Korean leadership and attend the first Central Asia-Republic of Korea summit, as well as a business summit session.

item.title: Kyrgyz citizens may soon travel to four Turkic countries using ID cards
item.description: Citizens of five Turkic states may soon travel within the organization using only ID cards, without international passports. This applies to Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Azerbaijan, and Turkey, with plans to expand the current agreement between Azerbaijan and Turkey. The Secretary General of the Organization of Turkic States confirmed ongoing preparatory work.

item.title: Tajikistan seeks investment for new solar power plants, discusses with China's LONGi
item.description: Tajikistan is seeking investment for the construction of new solar power plants. To this end, the country has discussed potential investment in this sector with China's LONGi company. Further details are expected.

item.title: Youth employment and career guidance event held in Namangan region
item.description: An event focused on youth career guidance and employment was held at Vocational School No. 2 in the Naryn district of Namangan region. The event included an open dialogue with young people studying professions like sewing, plumbing, and IT. Officials emphasized quality training and job placement.

item.title: Uzbekistan proposes reduced working hours for older employees starting 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan proposes introducing reduced working hours for women over 55 and men over 60, with preserved average wages, starting January 1, 2027. This measure is part of a draft presidential decree on pension system reform. The proposal also includes changes for self-employed individuals and the cancellation of social tax benefits.

item.title: Tashkent Hosts International Business Forum for Regional Cooperation
item.description: Tashkent served as a venue for an international business forum within the "International Leadership Awards" project. Entrepreneurs from Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan, Turkey, France, and Kyrgyzstan shared experiences and discussed future cooperation in various sectors including energy and tourism.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans Pension System Reforms, Expanding Funded Pensions by 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to reform its pension system and expand funded pensions by 2027. A draft presidential decree proposes increasing the calculation period for pensions from five to twenty years of salary history. It also introduces a mechanism to exclude 10% of a citizen's lowest earnings from pension calculations.

item.title: Tajikistan and South Korea Sign Industrial and Technology Cooperation Agreements in Seoul
item.description: During the first C5+1 ministerial meeting, Tajikistan and South Korea signed a Memorandum of Understanding on industrial cooperation and supply chains. The agreement aims to boost industrial infrastructure, trade, investment, critical mineral extraction, AI, and smart manufacturing technologies.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets with South Korean Prime Minister in Seoul to Strengthen Strategic Partnership
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with South Korean Prime Minister Han Duck-soo in Seoul. They discussed strengthening their special strategic partnership in trade, investment, technology, and transport-logistics, focusing on innovation, digital economy, and critical mineral processing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Launches "One Health" Project to Address Complex Risks
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has officially launched its component of the "One Health" initiative in Bishkek. The project aims to address complex risks, including infections, antimicrobial resistance, and climate change, by investing in biosecurity for economic benefit. The initiative involves regional governments and international organizations.

item.title: WHO official discusses 'One Health' concept and new infectious threats
item.description: A World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) official explained the 'One Health' concept, linking humans, animals, and the environment. He noted that 70% of human infections originate from animals, citing COVID-19 as an example. Preparedness for future pandemics is crucial.

item.title: Uzbekistan to gradually liberalize liquefied gas market
item.description: Uzbekistan will gradually liberalize its liquefied gas market, introducing market mechanisms. The reforms aim to ensure stable supply, efficient resource use, attract private sector investment, and transition to targeted social support. A new company, LPG-Trade, will be established.

item.title: Chingiz Akhmatov Appointed First Deputy Prosecutor General of Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Chingiz Akhmatov has been appointed First Deputy Prosecutor General of Kyrgyzstan. He was introduced to staff and expressed his commitment to strengthening the rule of law. The Prosecutor General's office now has five deputies.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Gradually Raising Retirement Age to 63 for Men, 58 for Women by 2039
item.description: Uzbekistan proposes gradually increasing the retirement age, reaching 63 for men and 58 for women by 2039. This plan, announced by the Ministry of Economy and Finance, also includes changes to pension calculation methods and increases in minimum work experience requirements.

item.title: Tajikistan Opens Digital Economy to Foreign Investors, Focusing on ICT and Green Energy
item.description: Tajikistan's State Committee on Investments presented a plan to attract foreign investors to its digital economy, prioritizing ICT, AI, energy, transport, and tourism. The period from 2025 to 2030 is declared the Years of Digital Economy and Innovation Development, leveraging the country's 98% renewable energy.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Partially Cover Diesel Fuel Costs for Agricultural Enterprises
item.description: Uzbekistan will temporarily subsidize a portion of diesel fuel costs for agricultural enterprises purchasing fuel through commodity exchanges. This measure applies to fuel bought between July 1 and December 1, 2026, if the price exceeds 15 million soms per ton. The subsidy is capped at 2 million soms per ton.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea Sign Key Agreements at Central Asia Summit
item.description: Uzbekistan and South Korea signed important agreements during a meeting in Seoul ahead of the first 'Central Asia-Republic of Korea' summit. The event focused on future cooperation in industry, trade, and technology, aiming to strengthen ties between regional enterprises and Korean businesses. Trade turnover between Uzbekistan and Central Asian countries/South Korea exceeded $10 billion in 2025.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets South Korean Companies on Automotive, Tourism, and Investment
item.description: Uzbekistan's President held meetings with representatives of South Korean companies to discuss projects in automotive manufacturing, tourism, and a $8 billion program. Discussions included developing the hotel business, producing electric and hybrid vehicles, supplying high-speed trains, and processing critical minerals.

item.title: Uzbekistan and UN Tourism to jointly prepare for the opening of the International Year of Sustainable and Resilient Tourism
item.description: Uzbekistan and UN Tourism have agreed to jointly prepare for the official opening of 2027, the International Year of Sustainable and Resilient Tourism. The opening ceremony is expected to take place in Tashkent in November 2026. An agreement was signed to define the organizational framework for the event.

item.title: US Confirms Deployment of Space Weapon for Defense
item.description: The U.S. Air Force Secretary confirmed the deployment of a space-based weapon for American defense against hostile actions. While details on its capabilities and deployment timeline were not provided, experts speculate it may involve electronic warfare systems rather than physical destruction of satellites. This move signals an intent to enhance military capabilities in space amid concerns about Russian and Chinese advancements.

item.title: Saudi Arabia and Yemen Seek US Aid Amid Houthi Offensive
item.description: Saudi Arabia and Yemen's official government have requested U.S. assistance due to intensified Houthi military actions. Yemen urged Washington to resume financial and material support for its armed forces and humanitarian programs, while Riyadh seeks direct White House attention. The diplomat noted that Houthi control over strategic Yemeni territories poses a national security crisis for Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Tajik and Swiss Scientists Discover Permafrost on Khargush Pass
item.description: Scientists from Tajikistan's National Academy of Sciences and Fribourg University have confirmed the presence of permafrost on the high-altitude Khargush Pass in Gorno-Badakhshan. Field geophysical research aimed to identify the depth and distribution of perennial ice sheets. The findings will aid in assessing the impact of climate change on the cryosphere and establishing a long-term monitoring system.

item.title: Tajikistan and EBRD Sign Memorandum for Energy, Transport, and Education Investments Until 2030
item.description: Tajikistan and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding outlining a strategic investment roadmap until 2030. The agreement focuses on sustainable energy, transport, and education sectors.

item.title: New Kia Model Production to Begin in Jizzakh, Uzbekistan
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev attended the launch ceremony for joint projects with leading South Korean companies and financial institutions in Jizzakh. Production of a new Kia model is set to commence in the region, signaling a significant step in automotive manufacturing collaboration.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea May Establish Industrial-Technological Alliance
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and South Korean Prime Minister Han Duck-soo opened a joint business forum. Over 300 representatives from government and business circles attended, including leaders from major Korean companies like Lotte Chemical and Hyundai Motor Group. The forum highlighted opportunities for increased trade and investment.

item.title: Uzbekneftgaz Prepares for Winter Season, Focuses on Gas Production and Supply
item.description: Uzbekneftgaz has begun a 30-day preparation phase for the autumn-winter season, focusing on gas extraction, well conditions, and stable supply. Despite significant efforts, some indicators remain below expectations. The company emphasizes the need for direct action at fields and wells to ensure gas availability for the public.

item.title: Chyngyz Akhmatov Appointed First Deputy Prosecutor General of Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Chyngyz Akhmatov has been appointed First Deputy Prosecutor General of Kyrgyzstan. He was introduced to the staff today. Akhmatov has worked in the prosecutor's office since 2004 and previously served as the Prosecutor of Osh region until his recent appointment.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Completes Construction and Renovation of 81 Schools for New Academic Year
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has completed the construction and renovation of 81 schools by the 2026-2027 academic year, according to the Ministry of Construction. Forty schools were built from scratch, and 41 underwent major renovations. Additional schools are nearing completion across various regions.

item.title: NABU to Assist Kyrgyzstan in Updating Red Book of Endangered Species
item.description: The German Nature and Biodiversity Conservation Union (NABU) will help Kyrgyzstan update its Red Book of Endangered Species. The project, funded with 21 million soms over 24 months, will use modern scientific data to assess rare species populations and threats.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Competition Committee Investigates WB Taxi Over Passenger Complaints
item.description: Uzbekistan's Committee for the Development of Competition and Protection of Consumer Rights has sent an inquiry to WB Taxi due to numerous passenger complaints. The committee noted an increase in complaints regarding taxi services, with nearly 20 related to WB Taxi reported between January and August. Issues include cars not arriving and lack of operator response.

item.title: One Kilogram of Psychotropic Substance Seized from Child's Electric Car in Bishkek
item.description: Kyrgyzstan authorities, with Russian cooperation, have intercepted a supply of psychotropic substances from Russia to Bishkek. A 20-year-old suspect was detained in Bishkek with a one-kilogram briquette of Alpha-PVP found in a child's electric car. The operation prevented the distribution of over 4,200 doses, with potential proceeds exceeding 4.5 million soms.

item.title: Turkic states' muftis adopt fatwa on artificial intelligence use
item.description: The 7th Meeting of the Council of Heads of Muslim Religious Boards of the Organization of Turkic States (OTS) in Baku resulted in the adoption of six fatwas, including one on the use of artificial intelligence in issuing religious rulings. Joint statements were also signed on family protection, Islam's stance on science and technology, and takfir.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Faces Potential Gasoline Shortages Due to Russian Supply Issues
item.description: Kyrgyzstan, heavily reliant on Russian gasoline imports, may face shortages. Russia is the primary supplier from the EAEU, accounting for 99% of Kyrgyzstan's imports in early 2026. Potential reductions or irregular supplies from Russia, due to domestic issues and export bans, could impact Kyrgyzstan's fuel availability despite EAEU exemptions.
